subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After the persistence race is repaired, should OpenClaw retain `turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` and the generic synchronous `onTaskTimeout` callback as permanent public/shared contracts?
rationale: The patch defect has a mechanical repair, but source inspection cannot decide whether a new operator setting and generic queue callback are the intended long-term ownership boundary rather than reuse of existing compaction timeout and release-signal controls.

options.title: Retain the new contracts
options.body: Keep the opt-in config and queue callback, repair persistence ownership, and add focused ordering and compatibility coverage.

options.title: Reuse existing lifecycle controls
options.body: Refactor the fix around the existing compaction timeout or queue release-signal mechanisms to avoid new public and shared surfaces.

options.title: Pause bounded maintenance
options.body: Defer this direction until context-engine cancellation and late-effect ownership are formalized.

recommendation.title: Retain the new contracts
recommendation.body: Keep the opt-in config and queue callback, repair persistence ownership, and add focused ordering and compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent merged work spans all three central surfaces: deferred maintenance, queue timeout behavior, and transcript rewriting.
